title: Descent of flat families with local complete intersection geometric fibres
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$, quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_{i_0}$-schemes $U_0,V_0$, and an $S_{i_0}$-morphism $g_0:U_0\to V_0$. For $i\geq i_0$ put $U_i=U_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, $V_i=V_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, and let $g_i:U_i\to V_i$ be the induced morphism; define $g:U\to V$ similarly over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $g_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $g$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the geometric fibre $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$. Here a scheme locally of finite type over a field $k$ is a local complete intersection if it admits an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras that are local complete intersections as defined in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; empty fibres are allowed. Then there is $i\geq i_0$ such that for every $j\geq i$, $g_j$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V_j$ the geometric fibre $U_j\times_{V_j}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$ in this sense.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), Situation (situation-descent-property); syntomicity expressed by flatness, local finite presentation and the geometric local-complete-intersection fibre condition, using Morphisms lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic and Tag 01UF (lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres), and Algebra lemma-lci-field-change. Persistence on a directed tail is base-change stability of syntomic morphisms.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1), $g_0$ is quasi-compact because $U_0$ is quasi-compact and $V_0$ is quasi-separated. Choose a finite affine open cover $V_0=\bigcup_a V_{a,0}$ so that each $V_{a,0}$ maps into an affine open $W_{a,0}\subset S_{i_0}$: such affine neighbourhoods form a cover and quasi-compactness selects finitely many. The definition of quasi-compact morphism makes $g_0^{-1}(V_{a,0})$ quasi-compact. Choose a finite affine open cover $g_0^{-1}(V_{a,0})=\bigcup_b U_{ab,0}$. These choices give finitely many triples $U_{ab,0}\to V_{a,0}\to W_{a,0}$. Their inverse images at every stage and at the limit remain open covers, since inverse image commutes with unions.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), first paragraph; finite affine covers as in its proof.

proof.text: Fix a triple, temporarily suppressing $a,b$. Write $W_0=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ and let $W_i\subset S_i$ and $W\subset S$ be its inverse images. The transition morphisms and limit projection are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes every $W_i$ and $W$ affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $W=\varprojlim_{i\geq i_0}W_i=\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R_i=\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O)$ and $R=\varinjlim R_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-tensor-comparison] to this fixed triple. It gives fixed $R_0$-algebras $B_0,C_0$ and a finitely presented $R_0$-algebra map $B_0\to C_0$, and identifies each chart morphism $U_i\to V_i$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R_i\otimes_{R_0}C_0)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i\otimes_{R_0}B_0)$, and the limit chart with the same formula using $R$. The identifications respect the displayed ring maps; no finite presentation of $B_0$ over $R_0$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), affine reduction, with Tags 01YX/01YW and Schemes Tags 01JR/01I4.

proof.text: The base change $g$ of $g_0$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3). Together with the given flatness and geometric-fibre assumption this is condition (1) of [lem-trf-syntomic-geometric-fibres-affine-criterion]. Its implication (1) to (2), applied to the affine pair $U\to V$ of each triple, says that $R\otimes_{R_0}B_0\to R\otimes_{R_0}C_0$ is flat and finitely presented and that every ordinary residue-field fibre ring is a local complete intersection. This checks the ordinary, rather than merely geometric, fibre hypothesis needed for the algebraic descent lemma.

source.place: Tags 01UD/01UE/01UF, with Algebra Tag 00SJ for the geometric formulation; Morphisms Tag 01TS for local finite presentation under base change.

proof.text: For each of the finitely many triples apply [lem-trf-syntomic-ring-filtered-colimit-descent] to the system $R_i$, the fixed finitely presented map $B_0\to C_0$ of step 2 and the three limit properties of step 3. Obtain an index $i_{ab}\geq i_0$ at which $B_{i_{ab}}\to C_{i_{ab}}$ is flat, finitely presented and has local-complete-intersection residue-field fibres. Choose a common upper bound $i$ for these finitely many indices and $i_0$. If there are no source charts, take $i=i_0$.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), second paragraph: apply Algebra Tag 0C33 (lemma-colimit-lci) on each affine triple.

proof.text:
Fix $j\geq i$ and a triple, and abbreviate $k=i_{ab}$. There is a canonical isomorphism $C_j\cong B_j\otimes_{B_k}C_k$: the map sends $(r\otimes b)\otimes(s\otimes c)$ to $r\alpha_{jk}(s)\otimes\varphi_0(b)c$, and its inverse sends $r\otimes c$ to $(r\otimes1)\otimes(1\otimes c)$; these formulas respect the balanced tensor relations and are inverse on pure tensors. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (1) give flatness and finite presentation of $B_j\to C_j$. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset B_j$, let $\mathfrak p\subset B_k$ be its inverse image. The induced field map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ gives the fibre identity
$$C_j\otimes_{B_j}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong(C_k\otimes_{B_k}\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q).$$
Both identifications are the associativity and cancellation of balanced tensors. The $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra in parentheses is of finite type, by finite presentation and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (1), and is a local complete intersection by step 4. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change] makes the fibre over $\mathfrak q$ a local complete intersection. This proves all three chart properties for every $j\geq i$.

source.place: Tag 00SN (lemma-base-change-syntomic), its three-line proof via flat base change, finite presentation base change and Tag 00SJ; tensor identifications written explicitly.

proof.text: At each $j\geq i$, the affine pairs of step 2 form the target cover $V_j=\bigcup_a V_{a,j}$ and source covers $g_j^{-1}(V_{a,j})=\bigcup_b U_{ab,j}$ of step 1. Their ring maps have all three properties by step 5, so they satisfy condition (3) of [lem-trf-syntomic-geometric-fibres-affine-criterion]. Its implication (3) to (1) gives that $g_j$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and every geometric fibre is a local complete intersection over its algebraically closed field. These are exactly the asserted conclusions, simultaneously for every $j\geq i$. Empty source covers and empty fibres are included in the criterion.

source.place: Tag 01UD (lemma-syntomic-characterize), (4) implies (1), combined with Tags 01UE/01UF and Algebra Tag 00SJ as in the affine criterion.
